questions.question: The zone where the earthquake waves are not observed is called:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Shadow Zone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shadow Zone** is a region on the Earth's surface where **seismic waves** from an earthquake are not detected.
 
• This phenomenon occurs due to the **refraction and reflection** of seismic waves as they pass through different layers of the Earth's interior.
 
• The **P-waves** (primary waves) are refracted by the liquid outer core and create a shadow zone between **104° and 140°** from the earthquake's focus.
 
• **S-waves** (secondary waves) cannot travel through the liquid outer core, creating a larger shadow zone that extends beyond **104°** from the earthquake's focus.
 
• The study of the shadow zone helps scientists understand the **internal structure** of the Earth, including the properties of the core.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Benthic Zone**__

 __
 
• The **Benthic Zone** refers to the ecological region at the lowest level of a body of water, such as an ocean or lake, including the sediment surface and some sub-surface layers.
 
• Organisms living in this zone are called **benthos**, and they include various species of invertebrates, fish, and microorganisms.
 
 
 
• **Hypocentre**__
 __
 
• The **Hypocentre** is the point within the Earth where an earthquake rupture starts.
 
• It is the location beneath the Earth's surface where the strain energy stored in the rock is first released.
 
 
 
• **Epicentre**__
 
 
• The **Epicentre** is the point on the Earth's surface directly above the hypocentre of an earthquake.
 
• This is the location where the earthquake's effects are usually felt most strongly.

questions.question: Which of the following is the national fruit of Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jackfruit**__.

*__Key Points__

__
 
• The national fruit of Sri Lanka is **Jackfruit**, known for its distinctive flavor and large size.
 
• Jackfruit is widely cultivated in Sri Lanka and is a staple ingredient in many traditional dishes.
 
• It is considered one of the largest tree-borne fruits globally, with some specimens weighing up to 40 kilograms.
 
• In Sri Lankan cuisine, jackfruit is utilized in various forms, including raw as a vegetable (e.g., "Polos Curry") and ripe as a sweet fruit.
 
• Jackfruit trees contribute significantly to local agriculture and livelihoods, being valued for their wood, fruit, and overall sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scientific Name:** The scientific name of jackfruit is Artocarpus heterophyllus*.
 
• **Health Benefits:** Jackfruit is rich in dietary fiber, vitamins (like vitamin C), and minerals, making it highly nutritious.
 
• **Ecological Importance:** Jackfruit trees are drought-resistant and adaptable to tropical climates, contributing to sustainable agriculture.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** In many South Asian cultures, jackfruit is considered a symbol of abundance and prosperity.
 
• **Global Popularity:** While native to South and Southeast Asia, jackfruit has gained popularity worldwide due to its versatility, including being used as a vegan meat substitute.

questions.question: Which sea separates Africa from the Arabian peninsula?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Sea.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red Sea** separates** Africa **from the **Arabian peninsula.**
 
• The Red Sea is a **seawater inlet** of the Indian Ocean, located between** Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.**
 
• It is over **2250 km long **and **355 km wide** at its widest point.
 
• The Red Sea is an important **shipping route**, connecting **Europe and Asia.**
 
• It is also a popular tourist destination, known for its** clear waters and coral reefs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Caspian Sea **is the **world's largest inland body of water**, located between **Europe and Asia.**
 
• It is bordered by five countries: **Russia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan.**
 
• The **Black Sea** is a sea between **Eastern Europe and Western Asia**, bordered by **Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Russia, Turkey, and Ukraine.**
 
• It is connected to the **Mediterranean Sea** through the **Bosporus Strait and the Dardanelles.**
 
• The **White Sea** is a southern inlet of the **Barents Sea**, located on the **northwest coast of Russia. **
 
• It is an important **fishing and shipping area,** as well as a popular tourist destination.

questions.question: Which among the following is the coldest of the atmospheric layers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M**esosphere

 
 
• It lies above the stratosphere, which extends up to a height of 80 km.
 
• In this layer, once again, the temperature starts decreasing with the increase in altitude and reaches up to minus 100°C at a height of 80 km.
 
• The upper limit of the mesosphere is known as mesopause​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **S**tratosphere

 
 
• It is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains the ozone layer.
 
• This layer absorbs ultra-violet radiation and shields life on the earth from an intense, harmful form of energy.
 
• The stratopause caps the top of the stratosphere.
 
 
 
• **Thermosphere ****​**
 
 
• It is located between 80 and 400 km above the mesopause.
 
• It contains electrically charged particles known as ions, and hence, it is also known as the ionosphere.
 
• Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• The temperature here starts increasing with height.
 
 
 
• **Troposphere**
 
 
• Its average height is 13 km.
 
• Troposphere is the densest layer of all.
 
• The air we breathe exists here.
 
• Almost all the weather phenomena like rainfall, fog, and hailstorm occur in this layer.

questions.question: What is the official language of Bangladesh, a neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengali.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Bengali **is the official language of** Bangladesh **and is spoken by the majority of the population in the country.
 
• Bangladesh was** previously known as East Pakistan,** and Bengali was recognized as an official language of Pakistan in 1956.
 
• After a long struggle, Bengali was declared the official language of **Bangladesh in 1971**, when the country gained independence from Pakistan.
 
• Bengali is also known as **Bangla,** and it is the **seventh most spoken language in the world, **with over 250 million speakers worldwide.
 
• Some other languages spoken in Bangladesh include** Rohingya, Chittagonian, Sylheti, and Rangpuri. **However, Bengali is the most widely spoken and the official language of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urdu** is the official language of Pakistan and is also spoken in some parts of India.
 
• **Dzongkha** is the official language of Bhutan and is not spoken in Bangladesh.
 
• **Hindi **is the official language of India and is also spoken in some parts of Nepal and Mauritius.

questions.question: The main minerals constituents of the continental mass are ________ and ________.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'silica, alumina'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silica (SiO₂) and Alumina (Al₂O₃):**

 
 
• The continental crust is primarily composed of silicate minerals, which are rich in silica and alumina.
 
• These compounds form the bulk of minerals such as feldspar and quartz, which are the most abundant minerals in the Earth's continental crust.
 
• Silica (SiO₂) contributes to the crust’s overall light color and low density, characteristic of continental rocks.
 
• Alumina (Al₂O₃) is a key component of feldspar minerals, which make up about 60% of the Earth's crust.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxygen and Carbon:**

 
 
• Oxygen is indeed a major component of continental crust minerals, making up about 46.6% of the crust by weight.
 
• Carbon, however, is present in much smaller quantities mainly in carbonate minerals, which are much less abundant in the continental crust compared to silicate minerals.
 
 
 
• **Silica and Magnesium:**
 
 
• While silica is a major component of the continental crust, magnesium is more prevalent in the Earth's mantle and oceanic crust.
 
• Minerals such as olivine and pyroxene, which are rich in magnesium, are found primarily in the mantle and oceanic crust rather than in the continental crust.
 
 
 
• **Alumina and Magnesium:**
 
 
• Alumina is a significant component of the continental crust, but pairing it with magnesium overlooks the dominant presence of silica in the continental crust rocks.
 
• Magnesium, similar to the previous point, is more associated with deeper parts of the Earth's structure such as the mantle and oceanic crust.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The composition of the continental crust is crucial for understanding various geological and geochemical processes.
 
• The predominance of silica and alumina gives the continental crust its unique characteristics, such as lower density and different mineralogy compared to the oceanic crust.
 
• This knowledge is fundamental in the study of plate tectonics, mountain-building processes, and the formation of different rock types.

questions.question: The holy mountain ‘Kailash’ is located in which neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **China**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mount Kailash** is located in the Tibet Autonomous Region of **China**.
 
• It is considered a sacred mountain in four religions: **Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Bon**.
 
• Mount Kailash is part of the **Kailash Range**, which forms part of the Transhimalaya in Tibet.
 
• The mountain is approximately **6,638 meters (21,778 feet)** high.
 
• It is near the source of some of the longest rivers in Asia: the **Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra, and Karnali** (a tributary of the Ganges).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Religious Significance
 **Mount Kailash** is considered the abode of **Lord Shiva** in Hinduism, and it is also revered in Buddhism as the home of the Buddha Demchok.
 
 

 Pilgrimage
 Every year, thousands of pilgrims undertake the **Kailash Mansarovar Yatra** to circumambulate the sacred mountain and take a dip in the nearby **Lake Mansarovar**.
 
 

 Geographical Location
 Mount Kailash is located near the **sources of four major rivers** in Asia, which are crucial for the water supply of millions of people.
 
 

 Environmental Conservation
 The region around **Mount Kailash** is protected to preserve its unique environmental and cultural heritage.
 
 

 Mythological Importance
 In Jainism, Mount Kailash is known as **Ashtapada** and is believed to be the site where the first Jain Tirthankara, Rishabhadeva, attained Nirvana.

questions.question: The first urban settlement to reach a population of one million was _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first urban settlement to reach a population of one million** was the city of **London **by around. A.D. **1810**.
 
• It was followed by **Paris **in **1850**, **New York** in **1860**, and by 1950 there were around 80 such cities.
 
• The rate of increase in the number of million cities has been three-fold in every three decades – around 160 in 1975 to around 438 in 2005.
 
• **London **is the city and **capital **of the **United Kingdom**.
 
 
• It is located 50 miles (80 km) upstream from the **River Thames'**s estuary on the **North Sea**, in southeast **England**.
 
• In the past, London originated from three main locations: the walled community established by the Romans in the first century CE on the banks of the Thames, now called the City of London, "**the Square Mile**," or simply "**the City**"; the suburb of Southwark, which is located across the bridge on the lower gravels of the south bank; and the City of Westminster, which is located one mile upstream on a large southward bend of the river.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In his seminal essay **"Cities as systems within systems of cities,"** **Brian J.L. Berry **(1964) established the** idea of the urban system**.

 
 
• The concept of urban hierarchy takes into account the differences in population sizes and economic roles among** metropolitan areas**.
 
• The primary focus of the examination of urban hierarchy is the ranking of cities according to many factors, including retail sales, industrial worker count, population size, and economic power.
 
• Rapid urbanization is a relatively new development. Few communities had populations of more than a few thousand people up until recently.
 
• The city of **London **became the **first urban community to have a million residents by the year 1810**. 
 
 
 
• Any **city **with a** population of more than 10 million people**, including its suburbs, is referred to as a **Mega city** or **megalopolis**.
 
 
• **New York**, which had a population of roughly 12.5 million, was the** first to become a megacity by 1950**.

questions.question: The Great Rann of Kutch falls into ________ region of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Thar Desert.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Great Rann of Kutch falls into the Thar Desert region of India.**
 
• **The Thar Desert is also known as the Great Indian Desert and is located in the northwestern part of India.**
 
• It is the **seventh-largest desert in the world** and covers an area of approximately 200,000 square kilometers.
 
• The Thar Desert is characterized by its arid climate, sand dunes, and extreme temperatures.
 
• The other options given in the question are not correct. The Coastal Plains are located along the coastlines of India, the Northern Plain is located in the northern part of India, and the Eastern Ghats are a mountain range located in the eastern part of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Great Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh located in the Thar Desert region of Gujarat, India.
 
• It is one of the largest salt deserts in the world and covers an area of approximately 7,505.22 square kilometers.
 
• The Rann of Kutch is known for its unique landscape, wildlife, and cultural heritage.
 
• It is home to several species of migratory birds, such as flamingos, and is also a popular tourist destination.

questions.question: Which of the following layers of the atmosphere means "region of mixing"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Troposphere.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The lowermost layer of the atmosphere with an average height of 13 km (16 km over the equator and 6 km over the poles).
 
• The air we breathe exists here. Almost all the weather phenomena (like rainfall, fog, clouds, dew, frost and hailstorm) occur in this layer.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height at the rate of 6.5℃ per 1000m. This is called normal lapse rate.
 
• The height of the troposphere varies from the equator towards the pole (decreases towards the poles) and from one season to another (increases during summer while decreases during winter) during a year.
 
• The upper limit is called the tropopause which is 1.5 km thick. (The word “troposphere” literally means “zone/region of mixing” and tropopause menas “where the mixing stops”.)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Stratosphere

 
• Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere. It extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomena, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains a layer of ozone gas between the height of 15 to 30 km (also called Ozonosphere).
 
• Temperature increases with height due to the absorption of UV rays by the ozone layer.
 
• The upper limit of the stratosphere is known as stratopause.

Mesosphere

 
• Lying above the stratosphere this is the third layer of the atmosphere and extends between 50 km and 80 km.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from space.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height again.
 
• The uppermost limit is the mesopause where the temperature becomes -80℃.

Ozone Layer

 
• The ozone layer is an area or a continuous region in the stratosphere of the earth that includes high concentrations of ozone(O₃) and protects the earth from the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

Thermosphere

 
• Temperature here rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The International Space Station is situated in this layer.
 
• It is further divided into two layers:

Ionosphere:

 
• It extends between 80 - 400 km.
 
• This layer helps in radio transmission. In fact, radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• Includes a number of ionic layers with increasing heights like the D layer, E layer, F layer and G layer.
